name: Flow remote-worker identity controls through defense supplier chains

attribution.legal_posture: First-party Lockheed Martin supplier guidance dated 2023-12-13. It is supplier guidance; statutes, regulations, procurement mandates, adjudications, and DPRK IT-worker incident disclosures involving Lockheed Martin or any named supplier or subcontractor require separate sources.

caveats: Apply the process proportionately and lawfully. DPRK affiliation requires evidence beyond nationality, accent, appearance, disability, camera behavior, geography, remote-work status, or any single inconsistency. Preserve human review and accommodations.

Nationality, accent, language, appearance, disability, camera behavior, geography, remote-work status, payment method, and any single inconsistency require corroboration before supporting a DPRK-affiliation finding.
Generalize the control rather than implying that Lockheed Martin, a supplier, or a subcontractor experienced an incident.
Unnamed organizations, suppliers, subcontractors, candidates, workers, and victims remain unidentified and outside inference.
Supplier guidance and industry proposals provide defensive context; incident-disclosure and DPRK-affiliation status require separate evidence.
The source's separate unnamed candidate-mismatch anecdote is attributed outside the North Korea case and remains outside the DPRK incident or lead record.
This is a governance control derived from supplier guidance; Lockheed Martin, a named supplier, or a subcontractor incident requires a separate incident source.
Use lawful, proportionate, privacy-preserving controls with trained human review, accommodations, documented reasons, bounded retention, and a meaningful correction or appeal path.

infrastructure.statement: For remote technical hiring and contracting, define interview, identity-verification, work-authorization, background, and work-location procedures; verify that they are followed; and require comparable screening requirements of subcontractors. Pair the flow-down with HR and hiring-manager awareness, routine control audits, remote identity management, participation in trusted industry/government information-sharing, and escalation to the prime contractor when concerns arise.
infrastructure.sector: defense industrial base and supplier chain

sources.support: Lockheed Martin describes identity-misrepresentation risk in remote hiring and contracting, expressly cites the U.S. DPRK IT-worker advisory, and recommends defined interview, verification, and background procedures. It tells suppliers to require similar requirements of subcontractors, train HR and hiring managers, audit awareness and new-hire screening, implement remote identity management, participate in industry and government information-sharing programs, and contact the prime contractor when assistance is needed
